beats.subline: Thursday, August 6, 2026 close — a modest pullback as Treasury yields rose, snapping the Dow's five-session record streak.
beats.body: Stocks slipped as the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.67% and investors weighed fresh earnings and labor-market data; semiconductor names like SanDisk fell sharply on AI capital-spending concerns, though all four major indexes remained well above where they started the year.

beats.headline: Uganda approves troop deployment to Trump-backed Gaza peacekeeping force
beats.body: Uganda's parliament voted Thursday to send troops to Gaza as part of the roughly 20,000-strong International Stabilization Force proposed by President Trump's Board of Peace, joining Morocco in committing forces; Defense Minister Kiryowa Kiwanuka cited Uganda's peacekeeping experience in Somalia, though opposition lawmakers raised concerns about the move.

beats.headline: Taiwan's president joins mock 'decapitation strike' evacuation drill
beats.body: President Lai Ching-te boarded an armored Clouded Leopard vehicle and was escorted to Taipei's wartime command center during the 'Wan Chun' drill, part of the island's largest annual Han Kuang exercises simulating a Chinese strike on its leadership; it is the first time Lai has taken part, following past participation by predecessors Tsai Ing-wen and Ma Ying-jeou.

beats.headline: Iraqi forces on high alert as militia deadline to retaliate for US-Saudi strikes expires
beats.body: Iran-aligned factions' week-long deadline for Baghdad to respond to the July 28 US-Saudi airstrikes on Popular Mobilization Forces positions expired Friday, and Iraq placed its military and security forces on heightened alert; the Islamic Resistance in Iraq has vowed retaliation against 'the American enemy,' while Iraq's ruling coalition has separately threatened terrorism charges against militias that don't disarm by September 30.

beats.headline: Rocket Lab wins $397M Space Force contract for airborne-threat-tracking satellites
beats.body: Rocket Lab will build, launch and operate a fleet of 'Flatellite' satellites under the Space Force's Space-Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator program, using AI-powered ground processing to give persistent orbital tracking of aircraft and missile threats in place of AWACS-style surveillance planes in contested airspace; the award is part of a $615 million package split among three contractors, following an earlier $4.16 billion SpaceX contract under the same program.

beats.headline: Anthropic slashes false positives in Claude's biology safety filters
beats.body: Anthropic rewrote the rule set governing Claude Fable 5's biology-related safeguards after gathering feedback from internal and external experts, cutting unnecessary refusals on benign queries like interpreting lab results or researching symptoms by about 85% in testing, while still routing genuinely dual-use topics like virology and molecular design to added scrutiny.

beats.headline: Bears activate LB T.J. Edwards from Non-Football Injury list
beats.body: Chicago activated starting linebacker T.J. Edwards off the Active/Non-Football Injury list, clearing him to rejoin practice after a minor muscle strain suffered training on his own following minicamp; Edwards, who had 67 tackles and a pick-six in 10 starts last season, will likely be eased back in after also rehabbing a fractured fibula from last season's wild-card game.

beats.headline: Byron says rare week off has his team confident heading into Iowa
beats.body: William Byron, still seeking his first win of 2026 after a 23-race drought, said the Cup Series' scheduled week off gave his No. 24 Hendrick Motorsports team fresh confidence ahead of Sunday's Iowa Corn 350, calling Iowa Speedway a track that has 'always clicked' for him after sweeping wins there across all three national series.

beats.body: No new PCA-specific development from a reputable outlet surfaced within the 72-hour window beyond the June General Assembly and stated clerk transition already reported in prior briefs.
